Through: Mr. Sunil Kumar G  the State.

The present petition filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of the FIR No.
257/2021, under Sections 498A/406/506 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Greater Kailash and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Neha Saini, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, South-East, Saket Courts, Delhi.
2. The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 23.11.2016 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.

sentences.text: 3. No child was born out of the said wedlock.
4. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately since October 2019.

1 Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant registered an FIR against petitioner no.1 (husband),
petitioner no. 2 (father-in-law), petitioner no. 3 (mother-in-law) and petitioner no. 4 (sister-in-law).

5. On 22.05.2023, parties arrived at a settlement before Mediation Centre, Saket Courts, New Delhi and as per the said settlement deed, petitioner no.1/husband has agreed to pay an amount of Rs.
2,00,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan, permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.

entities.text: Mediation Centre, Saket Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The copy of the aforesaid settlement deed dated 22.05.2023 is on record (Annexure P-2A).
6.

In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by a decree of divorce dated 16.09.2023, passed by Ms. Sukhvinder Kaur, Principal Judge (South-East), Family Court, Saket Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge (South-East), Family Court, Saket Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Further, as per the settlement deed, the total amount of Rs. 2,00,000/-
has been paid to her in Court today, by means of a demand draft.

7. Petitioners no. 1 to 3 and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and petitioner no. 4 through video conferencing have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, SI Neetu Yadav, PS Greater Kailash-1.

8. A demand draft bearing no. 548760 dated 13.02.2024 for Rs. 2,00,000/- drawn on Union Bank of India has been handed over to the complainant/Respondent No.2, who acknowledges the receipt of the same.
9. The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She further states that all the terms of the agreement have been complied with.

11. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ... In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."
